thread:
julia: quick heads-up — i'm planning a tf module bump for gpupool to address az-affinity and kms input shape. target rollout today during low traffic window.

mike: what's changing in the schema? any required rollbacks if something flaps?

julia: main user-visible changes:
- `subnet_map` becomes map(string) instead of list to make AZ binding explicit
- `kms_key_id` is now an object `{ id = string, alias = optional(string) }` (backwards-compatible via shim)
- added `az_preferred` default for pod placement

sam: shim sounds risky. How does GitOps handle the older clusters that still send `kms_key_id = "arn:..."`?

julia: we added a compatibility branch in the module: if `kms_key_id` is string, module wraps it into `{ id = kms_key_id }`. no state re-creation expected. Tests covered in CI.

anya: can we get an explicit canary workflow? prefer a staged rollout: apply to staging gpupool (1 AZ, dev namespace) -> smoke -> small dedicated capacity -> prod. also need helm values sync for nodeSelector changes.

sam: agree. i'll create a gitops PR that pins the module on the staging overlay to `ref=v2.4.0-canary` and leave prod pinned to `ref=v2.3.1` until we verify.

mike: what about IAM/KMS principal changes? last time we had a cross-account alias break during provider upgrade.

julia: no principal changes. only input shape. but the KMS alias parameter landing in the module will try to create an alias resource (conditional). we added a feature flag `create_kms_alias = false` by default.

deploy-bot: CI check — terraform plan for `infra/staging/gpupool` completed with 0 resource replacements. 

sam: nice. i'll run a targeted `terraform plan -var-file=staging.tfvars -target=module.gpupool` locally and post results.

sam: plan output snippet:
```
# module.gpupool.aws_autoscaling_group.gpu will be updated in-place
~ module.gpupool.module.subnet_map
```

anya: in-place is fine, but let's gate on metrics: queue length, pod start latencies, and spot eviction rate. if any exceed threshold, auto-rollback.

mike: how do we trigger rollback? do we rely on gitops rollbacks or terraform state roll-forward? i prefer reverting the gitops overlay then let the reconcilers converge.

julia: workflow: if metric alarm fires, ops runbook -> create PR to revert overlay -> merge -> argocd sync. i've added a note in the module README with explicit rollback steps and a small `kubectl` snippet to cordon related nodes: `kubectl cordon node/<node-name>`

sam: one more ask — add an acceptance test that applies both old and new input shapes to the same TF workspace to ensure provider doesn't try to replace KMS alias. i'll add it to pipeline.

anya: i'll update the helm chart values schema in the same PR so values schema validation won't block the canary.

mike: sounds good. keep me posted. i can standby to escalate to a rollback if autoscaler misbehaves. :thumbsup:

julia: thanks all — PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/compare/gpupool-module-v2.4.0-canary (opens in staging). will merge after 2h of green smoke tests.

deploy-bot: alert — argocd sync started for `staging/gpupool` (pr #432).
